sections.h2: What does the Webster County PVA decide, and what stays with others?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator is elected locally and assesses every real and personal parcel inside Webster County at fair market value. The PVA's office does not decide your bill. Two ingredients make it: the assessed value, which the PVA supplies, and the rate, which comes from the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and taxing districts such as the library board and health board.

Some property is valued in Frankfort, among it public service companies and bank shares, and the PVA's own page lists vehicles with them. The PVA may still change a vehicle's value for high mileage or a licensed body shop's estimate.

The PVA's counter is on the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Phone 270-639-7016, Monday through Friday, 8 to 4. The Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, shares the courthouse address, and its website carries a Property Taxes page for bill details.

sections.h2: When is the Webster County bill due?
sections.html:
The usual statewide timetable of KRS 134.015 applies. Pay everything by November 1 for 2 percent off. After that the printed amount stands through December, and surcharges start in January. The Sheriff stays the place to pay until April 15. If bills were mailed late, the Department of Revenue can instead run an alternative schedule, so rely on the dates printed on your own bill.

  • Early: through November 1, minus 2 percent.
  • Standard: the bill as printed from November 2 to year end.
  • Late, stage one: January, plus 5 percent.
  • Late, stage two: February through April 15, plus 10 percent.

After that, any open bill moves to the County Clerk, with a recorded lien and added fees. For a payoff after April 15, call the Clerk's office at 270-639-7006.

sections.h2: How fast does a late Webster County bill grow?
sections.html:
Quickly. Revenue's own example uses a $1,000 face amount. The Webster County Clerk's office handles delinquent real estate taxes under the same process, so the progression below is the one an owner should expect.

A $1,000 bill after it moves to the Clerk (Department of Revenue illustration)
StageTotal due
Transfer from the Sheriff, penalty and add-on included$1,254.00
Paid inside five business days$1,387.79
Paid after the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, two months of interest$1,627.61
Paid after the June advertisement$1,659.90
Bought by a third party at the sale$1,704.21

The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. The purchaser inherits the lien and may add its own charges.

sections.h2: What steps does a Webster County owner take to contest a value?
sections.html:
Talk to the PVA or a deputy before anything else, since the state bars appeals from owners who skip that meeting. The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office by close of business the next workday after inspection ends. The board wants documents: building and land details, insurance, construction costs, comparable listings.

  • The roll is displayed for 13 days beginning on the first Monday of May.
  • The board convenes roughly a month after display ends.
  • Taxpayers may make their own audio recording of the hearing.

A late-printed bill uses the value you claimed, with a supplemental bill following if the board sets a higher one. Paid agents must qualify under state rules and carry written authority.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Webster County?
sections.html:
Claim it at the PVA if you live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement plan. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

Webster County's Census median value is $112,900, which leaves $63,800 taxable. At the state's 10.6 cents per $100 for 2025, the state's cut falls from about $119.67 to about $67.63, with county, city, school, and district rates on top.

Disability claims need payments for the entire assessment period and a new application each year, unless the owner is a disabled veteran or has a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: Can I list a Webster County house with taxes behind?
sections.html:
Yes, but the debt does not disappear at the closing table. It belongs to the owner from the assessment date (KRS 134.015), and the lien outlives a sale for up to 11 years (KRS 134.420). Get written payoffs before accepting an offer: the Sheriff for this year, the Clerk for earlier ones.

The Clerk's site includes a delinquent tax lookup beside the land records. Should your certificate have been sold at the sale, the payoff goes to the buyer and includes that buyer's fees, so ask who holds it.

The sales contract normally divides the current year's bill by days of ownership. Make sure the split is written down and appears on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What is Webster County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Created in 1860 from parts of Henderson, Hopkins, and Union counties, Webster County bears Daniel Webster's name. Dixon holds the courthouse, while Providence is the largest of six cities that also include Clay, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft. It sits in the Western Coal Field and is the southernmost county of the Evansville, Indiana and Kentucky area. The county runs on Central time, and Wikipedia notes it was mostly pro-Confederate in the Civil War, with skirmishes and guerrilla fighting. Providence and Sebree voted to allow alcohol sales in 2018, and Clay followed in 2022.

  • 12,929 residents in 2025, a 0.7 percent drop from the 2020 base, spread over 332 square miles of land.
  • 5,772 housing units and 4,923 households of 2.53 people.
  • Owner-occupied homes make up 73.8 percent of the stock, valued at a median $112,900.
  • Half of households earn less than $59,628, and 16.1 percent of residents are in poverty.
  • Workers commute 28.7 minutes on average, longer than in neighboring Washington or Wayne County.

The county's population reached 20,974 in 1910, dropped to 15,555 by 1950, and stood at 13,621 in 2010. Owners pay a median $1,241 monthly with a mortgage and $405 without, and renters a median $783. The county has 202 employer establishments with 1,822 employees, and transportation and warehousing receipts of $51.3 million in 2022 outweigh health care receipts of $19.1 million. Only five building permits were issued in 2025, so houses change hands mostly as resales. Inherited homes, houses needing repairs, and those with tax liens can sell as-is for cash and clear the lien at closing.

The Census profile adds more texture. Residents 65 and older are 20.2 percent of the population and under-18s are 24.4 percent. Hispanic or Latino residents make up 9.0 percent, the foreign-born 4.4 percent, and 6.2 percent speak a language besides English at home. High school graduates make up 86.2 percent of adults 25 and over, and 12.8 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Just over 86 percent stayed in the same house for a year, 92.9 percent of households own a computer, and veterans number 527. Retail sales per person were $6,099 in 2022.

faqs.q: What are the Webster County PVA's address and hours?
faqs.a: On the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon. Call 270-639-7016 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the Webster County PVA decide my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The fiscal court, city governments, school board, and districts such as the library and health boards set rates. The PVA only determines assessed value.

faqs.q: By when must a Webster County appeal reach the County Clerk?
faqs.a: Before closing time on the workday after the 13-day roll inspection ends, and only once you have met with the PVA.

faqs.q: How much does the exemption lower a Webster County assessment?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 from the assessed value of your own home in 2025 and 2026, if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA handles the application.

faqs.q: Why does a Webster County bill cost more at the Clerk?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty and Sheriff's add-on are included at the handoff, then 1 percent monthly interest and commissions follow. Revenue's example grows $1,000 to $1,254 at transfer and about $1,611 after the first notice.
